# Roof racks, snorkels and storage

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Cut the ABS pipe to 8' 2" length.
2. Cut the front cross bar (EMT) to 8' 1.25" length.
3. Cut the legs (EMT) to 8' length each.
4. Drill four 1/4" holes in the front crossbar, two at each end on either side.
5. Ensure drilled holes are parallel by using a vice or drill press if possible.
6. [Partial] Drill one set of 1/4" holes near the top of both legs for bolt passage.
7. Screw the heavy duty tarp into the front crossbar at ten points using sheet metal screws and finishing washers.
8. Align screw lines approximately 90 degrees from the leg hole positions to allow wrapping around the bar.
9. Start attaching by making a pilot hole with a tiny bit, then inserting the washer and screw through it.
10. Attach one leg on each side of the crossbar so the assembly folds flat without interference.
11. [Partial] Secure the rolled-up awning to the roof rails using at least four hose clamps cranked down tight.
12. Drill two 1/4" holes in the top of the ABS pipe, measuring from the back end (2.5" and 94").
13. Thread a 5/16" bolt through the drilled holes from the inside to create a water-resistant attachment.
14. Glue an ABS cap onto the front of the pipe once the bolts are threaded in place.
15. [Partial] Fit a cleanout fitting on the back end, cutting a notch for the hex head if necessary.
16. Slide the awning into the ABS pipe and fit grommets over the 5/16" bolts to secure it with wing nuts.
17. Unroll the tarp fully and unfold the legs to adjust height by positioning them closer or further from the truck.

_Procedure reported by [t635]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/diy-hybrid-folding-and-rollout-awning.9383/>_

## Tips & gotchas

- Keep the initial screws tight. [t869]
- Wrap excess webbing over and screw it down to reinforce ends. [t869]
- [Partial] Use a vice or drill press to ensure crossbar holes are parallel. [t635]
- Measure the ABS pipe holes from the back end, not the opposite side. [t635]
- Drill pilot holes with a tiny bit before inserting screws through washers and tarp. [t635]
- Position legs closer or further away from the truck bed to adjust awning height. [t635]
- Add a center post to prevent the awning from flopping around. [t635]
- [Partial] Use tie-downs specifically for high wind conditions and night visibility. [t635]
- [Partial] Secure the outside edge completely to the front bar so it cannot flop. [t635]
- [Partial] Consider using two lines per pole due to the large size. [t635]
- [Partial] Add flagging tape to anchor lines so they do not become tripping hazards. [t635]
- Plan on using pins and drilling holes in the legs for permanent anchoring later. [t635]
- [Partial] Paint the mount for a finished look. [t474]
- [Partial] Consider a sliding setup where the lower portion drops to the ground like a fire escape. [t987]
- Use a top rung at the end of the ladder rails to hold sliders in place. [t987]
- Ensure bolts are long enough to pass through both the cargo door and the wooden board mount. [t941]
- Consider using washers or track mounts for easier removal without permanent holes in the deck lid. [t941]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Mounting directly to the plastic without reinforcement. [t245]
- Leaving the C-pillar plastic deformed after installation. [t245]
- [Partial] Drilling ABS pipe holes too small, which requires threading in afterward, [t635]
- [Partial] Resting weight directly on sheetmetal fenders without support, potentially crushing them under 200lbs of body weight. [t987]
